Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst.
Iran says that only diplomacy can end the war with the U.S. and Israel.
That's after President Trump rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and
stop the fighting, as NPR's Kat Lonsdorf reports.
In a post on social media, Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Rakhti wrote that Iran was
aware of President Trump's rejection and said that only "negotiated solutions" will end
the conflict now.
He also wrote that Iran is still waiting for an official U.S. response.
Trump told a group of reporters on Saturday that the Iranian plan was not acceptable but
did not give further explanation.
He suggested Iran wanted to make a deal because it's "desperate" and "losing so badly."
Iran made the proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz at the United Nations General Assembly
in New York last week.
The extended closure of the Strait has caused major disruptions to the world's oil supply.
Kat Lonsdorf, NPR News, Tel Aviv.
In the Northeast, one person is dead in a powerful and slow-moving nor'easter as it
moves along the eastern seaboard.
The New York Housing Authority says one of its employees was killed by a falling tree
in Brooklyn.
This says the storm pelted the Northeast with heavy rains and high winds that led to flooding
and power outages.
And Fitzsimmons owns a store on the Jersey Shore.
She says the storm did a fair amount of damage.
We had a full moon high tide, some bad winds, nor'easter.
And so we had a lot of water around the perimeter of the building.
High winds and tides along with heavy rains are possible, and they could cause flash flooding
along the east coast for the next few days.
In New Jersey, the first and only debate between incumbent Republican Tom Keene Jr. and Democrat
Rebecca Bennett is scheduled to take place tonight.
Keene is the lawmaker whose four-month absence from the House went unexplained until he disclosed
he was being treated for depression.
They're running for the district that includes President Trump's Bedminster Golf Club.
Keene's seeking a third term as Republicans work to keep their slim majority in the House.
Investors on Wall Street are bracing for the latest report card on the labor market this
week.
They're also watching for the Federal Reserve's favorite inflation indicator.
Trump hears Rafael Nam has more.
After raising interest rates this month, policymakers need to decide whether to raise them again
in order to bring down inflation.
A key factor will be the labor market, which has been remarkably sturdy this year.
If that trend continues when the latest numbers come out on Friday, it could give the Fed
more room to raise interest rates again.
After all, it's easier for households to absorb the impact of higher rates if people are employed.
In the week ahead, we'll also get the Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index, a key
inflation gauge.
Rafael Nam, NPR News.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
Hurricane Polo, which at one point was one of the strongest storms ever recorded in the
Pacific Basin, has weakened as it heads to northwest Mexico where it's forecast to bring
heavy rain and winds by tomorrow.
From Member Station KJZZ, Nina Kravinsky has more.
Officials in the Mexican states of Baja, California, Sur, and Sonora are watching conditions in
the Pacific as Hurricane Polo nears landfall.
The National Weather Service downgraded Polo but warned it remains a powerful storm.
Polo is predicted to make landfall in Mexico's Baja Peninsula on Monday as a less intense
but still strong hurricane.
The U.S. Embassy in Mexico warns travelers to be aware of flooding, mudslides, and road
closures early in the week.
For NPR News, I'm Nina Kravinsky in Hermosillo, Mexico.
Hurricane Nolo skirted Hawaii, but it could still cause flash flooding and dangerously
strong winds.
The National Hurricane Center says the storm is turning slowly south of the Big Island
and it's forecast to strengthen into a major hurricane late today into early tomorrow morning.
Hurricane watches have been canceled, but forecasters say parts of the Big Island could
see up to 20 inches of rain.
The Fat Bear competition in Alaska is almost over as people vote on which iconic brown
bear has gained the most weight ahead of the winter season.
The bears in Katmai National Park and Reserve, back on the pounds ahead of that winter high
expiration, which is key to survival, Gully, Walker, Backpack, and Becky are among the
competitors this year and the winter will be chosen this week.
I'm Janine Herbst and you're listening to NPR News from Washington.
